bullets.title: Semis sell off sharply; XLK on pace for worst month since Sept 2022
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks reversed early gains and turned down ~4% intraday on the China DUV news, with NVDA turning negative for the month after leading semis earlier. XLK is tracking its worst monthly performance since September 2022, while software (IGV) rallied ~3% on the session — a clean sector unwind.

bullets.title: China starts mass-producing domestic DUV lithography tools — the key catalyst
bullets.body: Per The Information, a Chinese state-backed firm has begun mass-producing homegrown DUV chipmaking equipment, with initial output targeting 5 machines this year and 20 by 2027. The news triggered ASML's 8% halt and broad chip equipment weakness; one analyst argued the panic is overblown given low near-term volumes, while another noted DUV demand remains additive rather than subtractive even with China's domestic push.

bullets.title: CXMT debuts +466%, hits $484B market cap — Goldman warns 'memory industry has a new problem'
bullets.body: China's CXMT surged 466% on its IPO debut to a ~$484B market cap, making it China's largest listed company and exceeding Intel's valuation. Goldman flagged this as a new competitive threat to the memory industry; CXMT also reportedly among the first Chinese fabs to receive domestically developed DUV machines in August. The combination of the IPO pop and domestic tool progress frames a structural bear case for Western memory names.

bullets.title: FOMC this week: 36% odds of a hike; unusual pre-meeting uncertainty
bullets.body: Fed funds futures are pricing a 36% probability of a rate hike at Wednesday's FOMC meeting — an unusually high uncertainty level for the days before a scheduled decision. Only 4 of 135 post-GFC meetings (3%) had similar pre-meeting ambiguity. Goldman expects the Fed to hold, but notes markets are pricing more aggressive action than their base case.

bullets.title: Global bond yields hit 2008 highs; 30Y Treasury at 5.17% — real-rate pressure persists
bullets.body: Global bond yields rose to their highest level since 2008, and the 30-year US Treasury closed last week at 5.17%, its highest weekly close since July 2007. The 2-year yield spread versus the effective Fed funds rate is now at levels historically seen before 500+ bps of cumulative hikes. Goldman separately warns this is a real-rate pressure story, not purely an inflation narrative.

bullets.title: Trump pushes for lowest global rates; touts Warsh, attacks Fed independence
bullets.body: Trump repeated calls for the US to have the world's lowest interest rates, called Fed board members 'political,' and expressed confidence that Warsh will 'do the right thing.' He also cited a recent strong inflation report and predicted prices will fall significantly post-war. Futures are only pricing 1.75 rate hikes by year-end, creating a wide gap between political pressure and market expectations.

bullets.title: Key macro week: FOMC, PCE, GDP data alongside peak earnings
bullets.body: This week stacks FOMC, PCE, and GDP prints alongside the heaviest earnings week of the quarter — AMZN, META, MSFT, AAPL all reporting. Goldman's quant desk characterized July as markets finally 'no longer ignoring' structural concerns beneath the surface, with oil volatility shifting investor focus from company earnings toward macro risks.

bullets.title: S&P 500 earnings beat rate strong at 86%; Morgan Stanley raises July ISM forecast to 53.8
bullets.body: Of the 135 S&P 500 companies that have reported, 86% beat EPS estimates and 69% beat revenue forecasts. Separately, Morgan Stanley raised its July ISM Manufacturing PMI forecast to 53.8 from 53.3, citing stronger Texas factory activity and rising new orders — though this morning's Dallas Fed print came in at 1.3 vs. 2.0 expected, a miss.

bullets.title: Durable Goods and Dallas Fed both miss; morning data sweep clean red
bullets.body: Monday's economic data was a clean sweep of misses — Durable Goods orders missed expectations and the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Activity index came in at 1.3 vs. 2.0 consensus (prior 0.0). Markets opened green before reversing, with NASDAQ erasing a 1%+ gain within 30 minutes of the open.

bullets.title: Oil tumbles 5%+ on Iran deal optimism; but Hormuz risks not resolved
bullets.body: Brent crude fell below $90 and dropped over 5% after Trump signaled he paused Iran strikes to allow talks, sending airline stocks higher and futures up at the open. However, Iran denied it is in peace talks with the US, the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted with nearly all merchant traffic on Iran-controlled routes, and US redirected 17 ships in the strait. Goldman flagged ongoing oil volatility as shifting investor focus to macro risks including inflation and higher rates.

bullets.title: US SPR hits lowest level since 1983 at 307.7M barrels
bullets.body: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve stocks fell ~3.7M barrels week-over-week to 307.7M barrels — the lowest level since 1983 — approaching the psychologically significant sub-300M threshold. This comes as Houthi drones targeted Saudi crude infrastructure and geopolitical risk in the region remains elevated.

bullets.title: NVDA invests $5B in Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence; gains access to next-gen Vera chips
bullets.body: NVIDIA committed approximately $5 billion to Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence (SSI) and announced a long-term partnership that gives SSI access to NVIDIA's next-generation Vera CPUs. NVDA is also reportedly in talks to provide a ~$250B backstop for an OpenAI data center project. Separately, NVDA options flow turned the most bearish on the session as the stock went negative for the month.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex trajectory: $426B in 2025 scaling to $1.4T by 2028
bullets.body: Top 5 hyperscalers are expected to spend $426B in 2025, growing to $600B+ in 2026, $1T+ in 2027, and $1.4T in 2028 — all driven by AI data center buildout. Moody's separately warned the 'unprecedented' AI capex is threatening the credit quality of AMZN, META, and GOOGL. Mark Cuban colorfully warned excess data centers will become 'pickleball courts,' citing private credit stress risk.

bullets.title: JPMorgan proprietary indicator flashes S&P 500 buy signal
bullets.body: JPMorgan analysts said an in-house indicator is now flashing a buy signal, one that historically correlates with S&P 500 gains. This comes as Goldman's quant desk simultaneously warns that 'July has been a long year' and that markets are no longer ignoring structural concerns — a notable divergence in major bank positioning signals.

bullets.title: Apple reclaims largest-company title; AAPL +16% MTD while NVDA turns negative
bullets.body: Apple reclaimed the world's largest company by market cap at ~$4.95T versus NVDA's ~$4.81T, a lead of approximately $130B. AAPL has rallied 16% month-to-date while NVDA has turned negative — a notable leadership rotation away from semiconductors and toward software and defensive large-cap tech.

bullets.title: NAND price weakness flagged as canary in AI stock trade coalmine
bullets.body: A note circulating highlights NAND price deterioration as a leading indicator of potential mean reversion in AI-driven semiconductor names, citing possible overcapacity and the view that AI stock rallies may be vulnerable. Chipmaker valuations are also noted to be higher than at the peak of the dot-com bubble, with one analyst warning that even if AI is revolutionary, price-to-value still matters.

bullets.title: China tariff cap set at 20%; current rate at 12.5% with upside risk
bullets.body: China claims the US agreed during trade talks to cap replacement tariffs on Chinese goods at 20%, up from the current 12.5%, implying room for tariffs to rise another 7.5 percentage points. Beijing warned it will respond to any new US measures and separately rejected US tariffs imposed on forced labor allegations.

bullets.title: CME launches Single Stock futures on 50+ major US names with near-23hr trading
bullets.body: CME Group officially launched Single Stock futures on 50+ of the largest US stocks and ETFs — including NVDA, AAPL, and TSLA — trading nearly 23 hours daily. The extended session allows traders to react to earnings and geopolitical news outside standard market hours, a structural market-structure shift.

bullets.title: Aug-Sep historically the weakest two-month stretch for S&P 500 over past 37 years
bullets.body: Historical analysis shows August-September has been the weakest two-month period for the S&P 500 over 37 years, with August-October producing the weakest average three-month returns. With multiple macro headwinds aligning — FOMC uncertainty, bond yield stress, geopolitical risk, and semiconductor sector volatility — the seasonal setup is a meaningful warning for bulls.

bullets.title: YouTube Premium bundles Peacock starting 2025; Amazon proposes 5,105-satellite LEO network
bullets.body: Google's YouTube TV will carry all Peacock content (live sports included) for YouTube Premium subscribers in the US starting early 2025, expanding GOOGL's content value proposition and providing a distribution win for CMCSA. Separately, Amazon's Project Kuiper/LEO proposed a constellation of up to 5,105 satellites targeting direct mobile connectivity by 2028, deepening AMZN's infrastructure ambitions.
